Which mosquitoes, and where they breed

MosquitoDiseasesWhere it breeds
Aedes aegypti, bites during the dayDengue, chikungunya, ZikaClean stored water: buckets, drums, flower vases and pot trays, fridge and AC drip trays, tyres, construction curing water
Anopheles stephensi, the urban malaria mosquitoMalariaOverhead tanks, wells, cisterns and water on construction sites
Culex, the night-biting nuisance mosquitoFilariasisPolluted water: open drains, septic tanks, blocked gutters

Aedes eggs stick to the walls of containers and can survive dry for months, then hatch when the container fills again. That is why emptying a container isn't enough; it needs scrubbing too.

Why fogging alone doesn't work

Fogging kills the adult mosquitoes flying at that moment. In warm weather a new generation goes from egg to adult in about a week to ten days, so if breeding sites are left alone, numbers recover within days. Fogging is useful for quick relief, but lasting control comes from dealing with breeding sites.

Our mosquito control programme

  1. Breeding-site survey. We walk the compound, terraces, parking, drains and construction areas, and list every place water collects.
  2. Source reduction. Containers that can be emptied, covered or removed are dealt with first.
  3. Larviciding. Water that can't be removed, such as drains, chambers, ornamental ponds and construction water, is treated to kill larvae before they become adults.
  4. Residual spraying. Shaded walls, stairwells, parking levels and dense plants, where adult mosquitoes rest, are sprayed.
  5. Space spraying. Fogging or misting of outdoor areas gives immediate relief when numbers are high.

During the monsoon, rain keeps refilling breeding sites, so larviciding has to be repeated regularly. For housing societies, offices and construction sites we recommend a scheduled monsoon programme from June to October.

Inspections and fines

Municipal health teams in Mumbai, Thane and Navi Mumbai inspect homes, offices and construction sites for mosquito breeding, and can issue notices and fines when larvae are found. A documented programme, with a treatment certificate after every visit, shows you are taking the required steps.

A weekly checklist for residents

  • Empty and scrub buckets, drums, vases and pet bowls once a week.
  • Cover water tanks and drums tightly.
  • Check the drip trays of fridges and air conditioners.
  • Clear terrace drains and gutters, and remove old tyres, coconut shells and plastic that collect water.
  • Fit mosquito mesh on windows, and use nets for babies and the elderly.
FAQs

Mosquito Control in Mumbai: common questions

Can you guarantee there will be no dengue cases?

No one can. Mosquitoes travel, and residents also get bitten outside the building. A good programme sharply reduces breeding on your premises, which lowers the risk.

How often should a housing society be treated?

During the monsoon, from June to October, larviciding and spraying are usually needed every one to two weeks. Outside the monsoon, monthly visits are usually enough.

Is fogging safe?

We use WHO and CIB-approved products. During fogging, close windows, keep children and pets indoors, and cover fish tanks and food that is outside.

Do you treat construction sites?

Yes. Construction sites are among the biggest breeding sources, and municipal teams inspect them closely. We treat curing water, lift pits, basements and debris that collects water, on a regular schedule.

How much does mosquito control cost?

It depends on the size of the compound and how many breeding sites need treatment. We inspect first and give an itemised quote.
